**Actionable comments posted: 9**
🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
ironic-config/apache2-ipxe.conf.j2 (1)
`22-24`: _💤 Low value_ **Consider tightening the FilesMatch pattern to specific boot file extensions.** The regex `^ironic-python-agent\.` matches any file starting with `ironic-python-agent.` (e.g., `.kernel`, `.initramfs`, but also `.evil.sh` or `.backup`). Based on context evidence from `ironic-common.sh` and `inspector.ipxe.j2`, only `.kernel` and `.initramfs` files are expected for IPA boot. A more restrictive pattern reduces the attack surface if an adversary gains write access to `/shared/html/images`.
🔒 Proposed tighter regex ```diff - + Require all granted ``` This explicitly allows only the two expected boot artifacts.
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@ironic-config/apache2-ipxe.conf.j2` around lines 22 - 24, Tighten the FilesMatch rule that currently matches any file starting with "ironic-python-agent." by restricting it to only the expected boot artifacts; update the FilesMatch pattern in the FilesMatch block (the one using "FilesMatch" and "ironic-python-agent") so it only allows files with the .kernel or .initramfs extensions (e.g., use a regex that matches ^ironic-python-agent\.(kernel|initramfs)$) and leave the Require all granted directive in place. ```
🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. Inline comments: In @.github/workflows/update-requirements.yml: - Around line 69-76: After assigning NGS_HASH from the curl|jq pipeline, validate the value and fail fast if the GitHub API did not return a valid SHA: check NGS_HASH (and likewise IRONIC_HASH and SUSHY_HASH) for empty or "null" and if so print an error to stderr and exit non‑zero; update the shell block that sets NGS_HASH (the curl ... | jq -r '.sha' pipeline) to perform this check immediately before writing to $GITHUB_OUTPUT so you never emit "`@null`" into requirements.cachito. - Around line 163-167: The workflow uses the wrong key name for the step output: replace the incorrect reference steps.current-hashes.output.current_ngs with the correct steps.current-hashes.outputs.current_ngs wherever it appears (e.g., in the format(...) calls that build the compare/Previous lines and in any Slack CURRENT_NGS usage); ensure all occurrences of "current-hashes.output.current_ngs" are changed to "current-hashes.outputs.current_ngs" so the published $GITHUB_OUTPUT value is read properly. In `@ironic-config/dnsmasq.conf.j2`: - Around line 38-42: The template emits raw DHCP options from env.DHCP_OPTIONS without validation; update the Jinja2 block that iterates env.DHCP_OPTIONS so each token is trimmed and validated before rendering: split on ";" then for each opt apply trim, skip if empty after trim, and reject/skip any token containing "\n" or "\r" (do not emit dhcp-option for those); reference the existing env.DHCP_OPTIONS usage and the for-loop in ironic-config/dnsmasq.conf.j2 and ensure only validated tokens produce dhcp-option={{ opt }} lines. In `@README.md`: - Around line 180-211: Update the README to reflect the actual wiring: state that IRONIC_NETWORKING_ENABLED gates both starting the ironic-networking service and rendering the ironic_networking_json_rpc/ironic_networking sections in ironic-config/ironic.conf.j2 (and that scripts/configure-ironic.sh treats true as enabling networking); note IRONIC_NETWORKING_JSON_RPC_HOST and IRONIC_NETWORKING_JSON_RPC_PORT are used in both ironic-config/ironic.conf.j2 and ironic-config/ironic-networking.conf.j2 (defaults localhost/8090); document that IRONIC_NETWORKING_ENABLED_SWITCH_DRIVERS and IRONIC_NETWORKING_SWITCH_CONFIGS map to enabled_switch_drivers and switch_config_file in ironic-config/ironic-networking.conf.j2 (defaults generic-switch and ${IRONIC_CONF_DIR}/networking/switch-configs.conf); clarify that the various *_NETWORK vars (including IRONIC_NETWORKING_IDLE_NETWORK) are only rendered into the [ironic_networking] section of ironic-config/ironic.conf.j2 when defined; and remove or reword the claim about switch-configs containing SSH keys since IRONIC_NETWORKING_SWITCH_CONFIGS is only passed as switch_config_file. In `@scripts/configure-ironic-networking.sh`: - Around line 12-33: Call wait_for_interface_or_ip() after sourcing ironic-common.sh (and before render_j2_config and before using IRONIC_IP/IRONIC_URL_HOST) so those variables are populated; specifically, add a call to wait_for_interface_or_ip() prior to invoking render_j2_config (which renders /etc/ironic/ironic-networking.conf.j2) and before exporting NO_PROXY, ensuring IRONIC_IP and IRONIC_URL_HOST are set for configure_json_rpc_auth and the NO_PROXY assignment. In `@scripts/runhttpd`: - Around line 86-90: The current validation in scripts/runhttpd (the if block checking "${HTTPS_IPXE_BOOT_DIR}" for *.{kpxe,efi}) only ensures at least one of .kpxe or .efi exists, which lets a missing BIOS or missing EFI path slip through; change the guard to validate BIOS and EFI firmware separately by asserting there is at least one *.kpxe present and at least one *.efi present in "${HTTPS_IPXE_BOOT_DIR}", and fail with an error and exit 1 if either check fails (use separate tests for *.kpxe and *.efi rather than the combined glob). In `@scripts/runironic`: - Around line 14-16: The script runironic calls generate_cacert_bundle_initrd to write /shared/html/ipa-cacert-bundle but never ensures /shared/html exists; update runironic to create the parent directory before that call (e.g., run mkdir -p /shared/html and set appropriate permissions/ownership if needed) so generate_cacert_bundle_initrd can always write the bundle safely and idempotently. In `@scripts/tls-common.sh`: - Around line 133-141: The current logic only enables IRONIC_INJECT_IPA when WEBSERVER_CACERT_FILE exists, which misses cases where only IRONIC_CACERT_FILE is provided; change the condition so IRONIC_INJECT_IPA is set to true if either WEBSERVER_CACERT_FILE or IRONIC_CACERT_FILE exists, then ensure IPA_CACERT_FILE is created/updated: if WEBSERVER_CACERT_FILE exists call copy_atomic to write it to IPA_CACERT_FILE, and if IRONIC_CACERT_FILE exists append it (cat >>) to IPA_CACERT_FILE; if neither exists set IRONIC_INJECT_IPA=false. Ensure references to IRONIC_INJECT_IPA, WEBSERVER_CACERT_FILE, IRONIC_CACERT_FILE, IPA_CACERT_FILE and copy_atomic are used so the bundle generation and ironic-config logic see the correct flag and contents. - Line 165: The cpio command currently appends to the bundle using >> "${output_path}", causing the archive to grow; change it to overwrite the file (use > "${output_path}") or, better, write to a temporary file and atomically mv it into place to avoid partial writes—locate the line containing the pipeline starting with "find . -print0 | sort -z | cpio" and replace the append redirection with an overwrite (or temp-file + mv) referencing the same ${output_path} variable. --- Nitpick comments: In `@ironic-config/apache2-ipxe.conf.j2`: - Around line 22-24: Tighten the FilesMatch rule that currently matches any file starting with "ironic-python-agent." by restricting it to only the expected boot artifacts; update the FilesMatch pattern in the FilesMatch block (the one using "FilesMatch" and "ironic-python-agent") so it only allows files with the .kernel or .initramfs extensions (e.g., use a regex that matches ^ironic-python-agent\.(kernel|initramfs)$) and leave the Require all granted directive in place. ```
